items.headline: US Stock Futures Surge on Easing Geopolitical Tensions; Big Week for Tech Earnings and Fed Decision Ahead
items.summary: U.S. stock futures are broadly higher this Monday morning, signaling a positive open as reports of a pause in U.S.-Iran military strikes over the weekend have significantly eased geopolitical fears and sent crude oil prices plunging. Investors are now turning their attention to a busy week featuring key Q2 earnings reports from major technology companies and the Federal Reserve's latest policy decision. Not financial advice.

items.statContext: Indicates a stronger open for the broader market.
Suggests a robust start for technology and growth stocks.
Points to positive momentum for industrial and blue-chip stocks.
Small-cap index futures also show strong gains.

items.headline: Nvidia Rises on OpenAI Funding and Partnerships
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) climbed 1% in early pre-market trading, driven by reports of potential involvement in a $250 billion financing backstop for OpenAI's Ohio data center and a new $500 billion partnership with SK Group.

items.headline: Outlook Therapeutics Jumps on FDA Approval
items.summary: Outlook Therapeutics ($OTLK) saw its shares surge 7% in pre-market following the FDA's approval of Lytenava for wet age-related macular degeneration (wet AMD).

items.headline: Oracle Posts Relief Rally on AI Infrastructure Hopes
items.summary: Oracle Corp. ($ORCL) shares experienced a 3% relief rally in pre-market, attributed to Nvidia's reported $250 billion OpenAI backstop, which traders view as a potential boost to Oracle's AI infrastructure business.

items.headline: Oil Stocks Decline as Crude Prices Plunge
items.summary: Occidental Petroleum ($OXY) fell 3.8% in pre-market trading, alongside other energy companies, as crude oil prices plummeted over 6% following reports of a U.S.-Iran military pause.

items.headline: Exxon Mobil Down Amid Falling Oil Prices
items.summary: Exxon Mobil ($XOM) shares were down 2.6% in pre-market trading, reacting to the significant drop in crude oil prices driven by de-escalating tensions in the Middle East.

items.headline: APA Corporation Shares Slip in Pre-Market
items.summary: APA Corporation ($APA) shares declined 4.73% to $34.44 in pre-market activity.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Decision, GDP, and Inflation Data Loom This Week
items.summary: Investors are keenly awaiting the Federal Reserve's July policy decision later this week, with markets largely expecting interest rates to remain unchanged. The week will also bring critical economic data releases, including second-quarter GDP figures and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index.

items.headline: Big Tech Dominates Heavy Earnings Week
items.summary: This week marks a crescendo for Q2 earnings season, with nearly one-third of S&P 500 companies scheduled to report. Notably, four 'Magnificent Seven' companies—Apple ($AAPL), Amazon ($AMZN), Microsoft ($MSFT), and Meta Platforms ($META)—are set to release their results, which will be closely watched for insights into AI-related capital expenditures.

items.headline: U.S.-Iran De-escalation Drives Oil Prices Lower
items.summary: Global markets are experiencing a relief rally as reports indicate a pause in military strikes between the U.S. and Iran over the weekend, causing Brent crude prices to fall over 6% to below $90 a barrel. This de-escalation is significantly reducing geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns.

items.headline: German Business Sentiment Improves, US Economic Confidence Rises Modestly
items.summary: German business morale exceeded expectations in July due to improved expectations, according to the Ifo survey. In the U.S., the Gallup Economic Confidence Index rose to -31 in July from -38 in June, showing a modest improvement in sentiment despite Americans remaining broadly pessimistic.
